PA-2025-HB2882.title: An Act providing for the protection of professional medical providers from interstate extradition due to providing lawful health care services.
PA-2025-HB2882.aiSummary: The bill would bar Pennsylvania officials from helping with out-of-state extradition, subpoenas, or other legal actions against medical providers over health care services that are lawful in Pennsylvania. It would also block state courts and licensing boards from enforcing out-of-state judgments, orders, or discipline based on those services, with a stated exception for medical malpractice claims under Pennsylvania law. The bill covers doctors, nurses, hospitals, and other health care providers, and it would also protect related patient and medical information from being shared with out-of-state authorities in these cases.

PA-2025-HB2868.title: An Act amending Title 75 (Vehicles) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in financial responsibility, further providing for required financial responsibility.
PA-2025-HB2868.aiSummary: The bill would lower the civil penalty from $500 to $100 for some vehicle owners or registrants who choose to pay a fee instead of serving a registration suspension. They would also have to pay the restoration fee and show proof of financial responsibility, which means car insurance or other required coverage. The choice could be used no more than once in a 12-month period, and the act would take effect in 60 days.

PA-2025-SR405.title: A Resolution honoring the life and expressing condolences to the family of Richard "Dick" Knoebel.
PA-2025-SR405.aiSummary: The Senate would honor Richard "Dick" Knoebel and express condolences to his family after his death at age 87. He led Knoebels Amusement Resort and also served in the Marine Corps, among other roles. The resolution is a formal statement of respect from the Senate.

PA-2025-SB1507.title: An Act providing for prohibited conduct involving algorithmic pricing structures and artificial intelligence, for enforcement by Attorney General and for civil remedies; and imposing criminal penalties.

actions.text: Referred to Consumer Protection & Professional Licensure

PA-2025-SB1507.aiSummary: The bill would make it illegal to use certain AI price-setting tools that rely on nonpublic competitor data, and it would also bar the use of common AI to set prices for goods or services sold in Pennsylvania. It would let the Attorney General investigate and bring cases, and it would let buyers who lose money sue for damages. The bill also sets criminal fines and says it would take effect right away.

PA-2025-SB1499.title: An Act amending Titles 23 (Domestic Relations) and 67 (Public Welfare) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in child protective services, further providing for employees having contact with children and adoptive and foster parents; and, in family finding and kinship care, further providing for definitions, for family finding required and for Kinship Care Program.
PA-2025-SB1499.aiSummary: The bill would change child welfare rules for kinship foster parents and family finding. It would update who counts as a relative or kin, require agencies to look for and notify relatives after a child is removed from home, and change what must be kept in the child’s case plan. It would also set clearer clearance checks and approval rules for kinship foster parents and spell out payment and public assistance rules for them.

PA-2025-SB1488.title: An Act amending Title 4 (Amusements) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, providing for temporary authorization of skill games.

actions.text: Referred to Community, Economic & Recreational Development

PA-2025-SB1488.aiSummary: The bill would let skill games be used in Pennsylvania for a temporary period. It would make the manufacture, sale, lease, distribution, repair, possession, placement, operation, and play of these games lawful, and people would not need a license or permit just for those acts. It would also block taxes or fees under this title from applying only because of skill game use. The temporary rule would end on April 13, 2027, and the bill would take effect right away.

PA-2025-HB507.aiSummary: The bill would require the state health department to test samples of baby food made in Pennsylvania for toxic heavy metals like arsenic, lead, cadmium, and mercury. It would set limits on how much of these metals can be in baby food sold in the state and require labels showing the test results. The bill says it would take effect one year after enactment.

PA-2025-SB922.aiSummary: This law changes the rules for private academic school licenses in Pennsylvania. It lets some schools apply before they have a building lease or final staff hired, if they include a plan and staffing projections, and it allows a short, temporary license approval for up to six months while some items are still pending. It also requires new rules for teacher and staff qualifications within 12 months and takes effect in 60 days.

PA-2025-SB908.aiSummary: The law updates Pennsylvania’s Prevailing Wage Act for public works projects. It adds rules for custom fabrication, which is off-site work made for a specific project, and says those workers must be paid the same prevailing wage used for the project. It also makes firms doing custom fabrication follow the same reporting, compliance, and penalty rules as other contractors, and it took effect 60 days after passage.

PA-2025-SB1334.aiSummary: The law updates Pennsylvania’s medical practice rules and adds new licenses for medical imaging professionals, radiation therapists, radiologist assistants, and trainees. It sets education, exam, age, and character rules for these jobs, and says some of these workers may perform certain imaging or therapy tasks under set limits or supervision. It also changes rules for several other licensed health jobs and removes older rules on some radiologic procedures and training.
